verdicts.note: Pamphlet and site statements ("standing firm against new taxes") [S1][S2], ESHB 2081/ESSB 5814 nays [S8][S9] and narrowing/sunset amendments [S6][S7]; roll call re-checked (Jacobsen nay).

The "top-down mandates from out-of-touch politicians who ignore our rural communities" line [S3] is general campaign framing in a biographical passage; it names no state mandate, zoning, growth-management or regional-authority issue. Direction plausible, evidence indirect: lower to low.
Flock camera ban, data-harvesting limits and data centers paying grid costs [S4] are pole_b specifics.

missing.basis: Her site says "many of our local issues are best addressed at the state and regional level: homelessness and the dual problems of mental health and addiction; equitable traffic funding south of Seattle; and job creation" [S2], a single clear statement toward the regional/state pole.
Would keep local clinics and hospitals open, cap prescription drug prices, and expand mental-health and addiction treatment [S4]: within-system measures (pole_a), with no single-payer plank.
